**sdd/issue-231-a2/apply-progress**

**What**: CP-A2a review-remediation batch for issue #231 A2, on branch `feat/issue-231-a2-pr3` (final tranche, off merged `feature/v2.0.0`). Fixed M1 (MAJOR, closing-keyword vocabulary divergence), m2 (MINOR, issue-number extraction precedence), m4 (MINOR, drift-guard env vocabulary gap) with strict TDD RED→GREEN; documented m3 (MINOR, actor-check gh-hardcoded on GitLab) as a known gap in design.md without changing code, per the ruling. All prior A2 apply-progress (phases 1-5, commits 660b950/dc78d27/46fdea1/f332c41) remains complete and unaffected — this is a NEW commit on top, not a revision of those.

**Why**: CP-A2a PR review surfaced a real fail-closed parity divergence (`issueLink()`'s narrow 3-form closing-keyword regex vs GitHub bash's/actor-check.mjs's broad 9-form vocabulary — `Fixed #42` passed bash but failed the Node REQUIRED gate), an issue-number extraction precedence mismatch on slice targets (Node always resolved the closing ref first; bash resolves Part-of first), and a drift-guard blind spot (the negative-space env-var guard was never extended to cover the addendum's own new `DEFAULT_BRANCH`/`CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH` seam vars).

**Where** (commit 2ef6bdd, 8 files, 277 insertions/33 deletions):
- `brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-ref-patterns.mjs` (NEW) — the ONE shared pure-constant module: `CLOSING_RE = /\b(close[sd]?|fix(?:e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)\s+#(\d+)/i` (all 9 GitHub-documented forms, capture group 2 = issue number) and `CHAIN_RE = /\bpart\s+of\s+#(\d+)/i` (capture group 1 = issue number). No ci-context import — REQ-CIC-4 holds (pure evaluators may import a sibling pure-constants module; the guard is against the ci-context SEAM, not against unifying pure regex constants).
- `brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-link.mjs` — deleted its own narrow local `CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE`, now imports the shared broad pattern. `issueLink()`'s verdict WIDENS (accepts all 9 forms now, was 3). Reason string updated to describe the broader vocabulary while still containing "Part of" (existing test dependency).
- `brain/scripts/governance/checks/issue-link.test.mjs` — 5 new RED→GREEN tests: `Fixed #42`, `Close #10`, `Closed #3`, `Resolved #5`, `resolve #8` all → pass. 12/12 (was 7).
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.mjs` — deleted local `CLOSING_NUM_RE`/`CHAIN_NUM_RE` duplicates, imports shared `CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE`. `extractIssueNumber(body, closingRequired)` signature changed (now takes the already-computed `closingRequired` boolean from `requiresClosingKeyword(ctx)`): on a DEFAULT-branch target (`closingRequired===true`) only the closing pattern is consulted (mirrors bash's base==main branch, no Part-of fallback there); on a SLICE target, Part-of is tried FIRST then closing (mirrors bash's base!=main branch exactly — governance.yml:66-76). Docstring's false "SAME precedence as issueLink()" claim removed/corrected. The `!CLOSING_NUM_RE.test(...)` default-branch-policy check now uses the shared `CLOSING_RE`.
- `brain/scripts/governance/run-check.test.mjs` — 1 new m2 RED→GREEN test (body with BOTH `Closes #42` AND `Part of #7` on a slice target → asserts `fetchIssue` is called with `7`, not `42`, matching bash's Part-of-first slice precedence). 4 new M1 parity-table rows (`Fixed #N`, `close #N`, `Resolved #N` all PASS on both paths; PLUS the exact M1 case `Fixed #42` targeting the DEFAULT branch → PASS on both paths, the row that was previously impossible before the widen+precedence fix landed together). Truth-table header comment updated with a "VOCABULARY DIMENSION" note. 52/52 in this file (was 47 pre-fix, 4 new-row RED + 1 m2 RED = 5 failures confirmed before implementation).
- `brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.mjs` — deleted its own `CLOSING_KEYWORD_RE`/`PART_OF_RE` (these were ALREADY the broad 9-form vocabulary, behaviorally identical to the new shared pattern), imports shared `CLOSING_RE`/`CHAIN_RE` instead. Group-index references updated (`m[1]`→`m[2]` for `CLOSING_RE` since the shared regex's group 2 is the number, group 1 is the keyword; `CHAIN_RE`'s group 1 is unchanged). Pure refactor — 38/38 existing tests still pass unchanged (behavior-preserving, confirmed before AND after).
- `brain/scripts/vcs/ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs` — `PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN` extended with `|DEFAULT_BRANCH|CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH` alternation. 1 new RED→GREEN test asserting the pattern now matches `process.env.DEFAULT_BRANCH` / `process.env.CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH`. 24/24 (was 23 pre-fix, 1 RED confirmed).
- `openspec/changes/issue-231-a2/design.md` — two new subsections: "Decision 2 ADDENDUM 2 (M1)" registers the precedent ("pure evaluator unchanged" / REQ-CIC-4 protects against refactor-drift, NOT against a ruled correctness fix — the evaluator accepted FEWER forms than the platforms honor, a pre-existing bug); "Known gap (m3)" documents `actor-check.mjs`'s `gh`-hardcoded fetch as an intentional DETECTION-only degrade-safe scope boundary, destined for CP-A2b/A3's provider-verb abstraction, NOT fixed in this slice.

**Learned**:
- REGEX STATEFULNESS GOTCHA discovered while writing the m4 RED test: `PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN` carries the `g` flag. `assert.match()` internally calls `RegExp#test()`, which on a GLOBAL regex mutates `lastIndex` across calls — asserting `assert.match('process.env.DEFAULT_BRANCH', PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN)` then `assert.match('process.env.CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH', PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN)` in the SAME test made the second assertion spuriously FAIL (lastIndex advanced past the shorter second string's length). Confirmed via a standalone repro before writing the real test. Fixed by using `String#match()` instead (which resets `lastIndex` to 0 internally on every call, per spec) — matching how the file's OWN pre-existing assertions already use `src.match(PIPELINE_ENV_PATTERN)`, never `assert.match`/`.test()`, on this specific global regex. Reusable gotcha: never `assert.match()` (or raw `.test()`) a shared global-flagged regex object across multiple assertions in the same test — use `String#match()` or a fresh `RegExp` instance instead.
- The M1 fix required touching BOTH `issue-link.mjs` (the pure evaluator's pass/fail check) AND `run-check.mjs` (its own separately-duplicated `CLOSING_NUM_RE` used for the default-branch closing-keyword POLICY check and issue-number extraction) — widening only one would have left the other half of the parity gap open. The exact M1 parity-table row (`Fixed #42` to default branch) only goes green when both fixes land together; it was used as the integration-level proof, not just the unit-level `issueLink()` tests.
- `CLOSING_RE`'s shared regex group indices differ from what each of the three original files used to use (`issue-link.mjs`'s old version had NO capture groups at all — boolean-only; `run-check.mjs`'s old `CLOSING_NUM_RE` had the number at group 1 via a non-capturing keyword group; `actor-check.mjs`'s old `CLOSING_KEYWORD_RE` also had the number at group 1). The new shared regex captures the KEYWORD at group 1 (needed nowhere directly, but keeping it capturing rather than non-capturing was a deliberate design choice for readability) and the NUMBER at group 2 — every importer needing the number was updated to reference `match[2]`, not `match[1]`.
- Verified via `git show --stat` on the sibling C4 review-fix commit (`f7b5ae0`, "fix(memory): address C4 review") that review-remediation commits do NOT touch `tasks.md` — precedent followed here: `tasks.md` left untouched (these findings were never task-list items, they're PR-review findings).

Full `npm test`: 1132/1132 pass, 0 failures (baseline before this batch was 1121; +11 new tests: 5 issue-link.test.mjs + 5 run-check.test.mjs (4 parity rows + 1 m2 precedence test) + 1 ci-context-drift-guard.test.mjs). `repo:check` and `brain:nav` both clean. Commit `2ef6bdd` "fix(governance): unify closing-keyword vocabulary (9 forms, shared) + issue-num precedence + drift-guard env (A2 CP-A2a review) (#231)" on branch `feat/issue-231-a2-pr3`, ONE commit, no push, no PR (per instructions). `brain/core/` untouched this batch (no L6 brain-writes-reviewed gate engagement needed). `.memory/` and `docs/inbox/PLAN-adapters-v3.md` deliberately excluded from staging.
